text: For finite-dimensional V, the map ι: V → V** defined by ι(v)(f) = f(v) is an isomorphism.
explanation: ι is injective (a nonzero vector admits a functional not vanishing on it) and dim V** = dim V* = dim V, so it is an isomorphism. Unlike V ≅ V*, it requires no choice of basis — this is the sense in which double duality is canonical.
